overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of Heidegger's account of how a world is disclosed. You'll be asked about attunement and thrownness, fear and anxiety, understanding as projection, the care structure, and the "they."

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: On Heidegger's account, what do moods primarily disclose?

options.html: A private inner state that colors an otherwise neutral world
options.text: A private inner state that colors an otherwise neutral world
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Heidegger denies that moods are inner states laid over a neutral world. They disclose being-in-the-world as a whole.

options.html: Nothing, since moods only distort what cognition reveals
options.text: Nothing, since moods only distort what cognition reveals
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. For Heidegger, moods disclose the world more basically than cognition does.

options.html: Being-in-the-world as a whole, and Dasein's thrownness
options.text: Being-in-the-world as a whole, and Dasein's thrownness
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Moods disclose thrownness and being-in-the-world as a whole, and they make it possible for things to matter.

options.html: One particular object that the mood is about
options.text: One particular object that the mood is about
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Moods aren't directed at one object. They disclose being-in-the-world as a whole.

forms.stemHtml: How does anxiety differ from fear in Heidegger's analysis?

options.html: Anxiety is stronger than fear, but has the same kind of object
options.text: Anxiety is stronger than fear, but has the same kind of object
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The difference isn't intensity. Fear is of something definite in the world. Anxiety has no definite object.

options.html: Fear is of something definite; anxiety discloses the world as such
options.text: Fear is of something definite; anxiety discloses the world as such
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! In anxiety, nothing in particular threatens. The world as such, and Dasein's own being-in-the-world, are disclosed.

options.html: Fear is a mood, but anxiety is a judgment about the future
options.text: Fear is a mood, but anxiety is a judgment about the future
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Both are moods. Fear is of something definite; anxiety has no definite object and discloses the world as such.

options.html: Anxiety concerns other people, while fear concerns things
options.text: Anxiety concerns other people, while fear concerns things
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The difference is between a definite object (fear) and no definite object (anxiety).

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are moments of care, on Heidegger's account? (Select all that apply.)

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is existentiality: Dasein's being out ahead of itself in its possibilities.
Correct! This is facticity: Dasein always already finds itself thrown into a world.

options.html: Being alongside the beings it encounters
options.text: Being alongside the beings it encounters
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is falling: Dasein's everyday absorption in its concerns.

options.html: Worrying about the welfare of others
options.text: Worrying about the welfare of others
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Care in Heidegger's sense isn't worry or concern for others. It's the formal unity of Dasein's being.

options.html: Reflecting on one's own mental states
options.text: Reflecting on one's own mental states
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Reflection on mental states isn't a moment of care. Care's moments are ahead-of-itself, already-in-the-world, and alongside the beings encountered.

forms.stemHtml: Heidegger says understanding throws Dasein forward onto possibilities, which it lives toward without making them thematic. What is his term for this structure of understanding? Enter one word.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Understanding has the structure of projection (Entwurf): Dasein is thrown forward onto possibilities.
Sorry, that's incorrect. Interpretation develops understanding by making it explicit. The forward-throwing structure of understanding itself is projection.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Heidegger calls this structure of understanding projection (Entwurf).

forms.stemHtml: A graduate student chooses a thesis topic mainly because it's "what one works on" in the field, without asking whether it's their own question. Which of Heidegger's concepts best describes this?

options.html: Anxiety, since the student is afraid of choosing wrongly
options.text: Anxiety, since the student is afraid of choosing wrongly
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Nothing here involves anxiety. The student's choice is shaped by what "one" does, which is Heidegger's "they."

options.html: Projection, since the student has chosen a possibility
options.text: Projection, since the student has chosen a possibility
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Every choice involves projection. What's distinctive here is that the possibility is taken over from what "one" does, which is the "they."

options.html: The "they," whose norms set what anyone does
options.text: The "they," whose norms set what anyone does
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The student understands their possibilities in terms of what "one" does. Heidegger calls this anonymous public "one" the "they."

options.html: Thrownness, since the student didn't choose the field
options.text: Thrownness, since the student didn't choose the field
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The student does choose, but in the terms of what "one" does. That's the "they."

title: Mood, Understanding, and Care
